text: Asim Ahmed Khan is an Indian politician from Delhi and a former cabinet minister in the Delhi government, serving in the ministries of Food and Civil Supply, Environment and Forest, Minority Affairs, and Elections. He was a member of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and represented the Matia Mahal Assembly constituency in the 6th Delhi Assembly. Born in Delhi, he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from Chaudhary Charan Singh University. He is a member of the AAP minority wing and contested the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) elections in 2012, receiving 6,300 votes. The AAP party website notes that he has worked in the Old Delhi area for 12 years and participated in various social activities. In the 2015 Delhi Legislative Assembly elections, Khan contested as an AAP candidate from Matia Mahal, raising issues of education and health. He won the seat with 47,584 votes, defeating five-time MLA Shoaib Iqbal, who ran on an Indian National Congress ticket, by a margin of 26,096 votes. Khan was described as a "less acknowledged 'giant killer'" despite having a "poor experience in politics," as Shoaib Iqbal had previously won five times, including in 2013 on a Janata Dal (United) ticket. The AAP secured 67 out of 70 seats in the Delhi assembly. Khan was one of four Muslim MLAs in the Sixth Legislative Assembly of Delhi and was considered "key" to AAP's success, which captured 80% of the Muslim vote. The AAP's minority wing played a crucial role in shifting Muslim votes—traditionally going to Congress—from Congress to AAP, contributing to AAP's decisive victory. Khan was sworn in as a cabinet minister on 14 February 2015 under Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, being assigned responsibility for the Food and Civil Supply, Environment and Forest, Minority Affairs, and Elections ministries. On 9 October 2015, Kejriwal dismissed Khan from the cabinet on corruption charges, specifically for allegedly cutting a deal worth Rs. 6 lakh with a local builder. However, Khan was later cleared by the CBI due to lack of evidence.
